subject: Custom SLA addendum & order form language (Meditech Solutions)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <procurement@meditechsolutions.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Meditech Solutions Legal <legal@meditechsolutions.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for Redwood deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about the potential for Redwood to power our clinical decision support pipelines. Procurement/Legal have a handful of contract items we need to lock down before we can proceed with the Dedicated deployment. Primary asks:

- A bespoke SLA addendum exhibiting a 99.99% monthly availability commitment for the API endpoints used by our production environment (Region: us-west-2).
- A p95 inference latency target of <=250ms for single-request text-generation (token length baseline provided below) and a p99 commitment for batching workloads when using dedicated capacity.
- Explicit regional failover behavior and mean-time-to-failover (MTTF) for cross-region routing.
- Service credit schedule tied to calendar-month uptime (we've proposed a 10% credit for >=99.95% and <99.99%, 25% for >=99.9% and <99.95%, etc.).

Procurement also needs: evidence that the uptime/latency commitments are realistic for our workload (we can share traffic profiles), an operations runbook excerpt showing incident escalation and notification windows, and any SOC2/attestation artifacts that cover monitoring and incident logs. Native order form language for inclusion in our MSA/SOW is preferred (we want explicit exhibit text to drop into our template).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (1) a draft SLA exhibit (redlineable), (2) an evidence matrix that maps Redwood observability/alerts to the uptime calculation, and (3) a recommended fallback model/route in the event of capacity constraints? We are targeting a procurement review by 6/28 — if you can share drafts by 6/18 that would keep us on schedule.

I've attached a short note that summarizes our desired credit schedule and a sample traffic distribution (attachment: meditech_initial_sla_request.pdf [pdf]).

Regards,
Laura Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Meditech Solutions

--
Attachment: meditech_initial_sla_request.pdf [pdf]
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Laura Chen <procurement@meditechsolutions.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for Redwood deployment

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask and the packet. We're happy to collaborate on an SLA exhibit and the corresponding evidence pack. High level response and proposed plan:

1) Draft SLA exhibit: yes — we'll produce an initial redlineable exhibit that covers uptime measurement, credits, and order form callouts. Target delivery: 6/18 (we can iterate).

2) Evidence matrix & operations runbook excerpt: yes — Ops will provide a scannable matrix linking metrics (uptime, p95/p99 latency) to our monitoring signals (routing, region health, GPU pool capacity). We'll also include incident notification windows and on-call escalation paths.

3) Fallback model: recommend a two-tier approach — primary dedicated pool (pinned model/quantization profile) + a defined fallback variant (lower resource profile / higher latency) with explicit routing policy. We'll document automated fallback triggers and regional failover MTTF estimates.

Two quick clarifying asks to help scope the draft:
- Can you confirm typical token-length distribution for the p95/p99 latency targets and expected QPS per region? The attachment helped but we'll need a little more granularity for batching assumptions.
- Are you intending to rely on committed Dedicated capacity (reserved) or want Redwood-hosted as the primary with a Dedicated hybrid? That changes the ordering/orderform language.

I've looped in Naomi (sales lead on this deal) and David (ops/product) to draft the exhibit and evidence matrix. We'll aim to share: Redwood draft exhibit v0.1, an evidence matrix spreadsheet, and suggested order form language by 6/18. If that's acceptable I'll mark the deliverables in HubSpot and attach the DocuSign stub once legal signs off.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for Redwood deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks — that timeline works on our side. To clarify the two questions:

- Token distribution: ~70% of requests are short (<=60 tokens), 25% mid (61-300 tokens), 5% long (>300 tokens). Most requests are single-turn synchronous calls; expected baseline QPS in production is 12 sustained with peaks to ~65 for brief windows.
- Capacity model: procurement prefers a dedicated reserved pool for baseline throughput with the ability to burst to hosted capacity; we need the order form to reflect that hybrid behavior and how credits are calculated if fallback is used.

Also, per our legal team: please include explicit language for (a) regional failover (which regions Redwood will support), (b) proof of observability (API that returns uptime calculations and incident history), and (c) an audit window for evidence requests (e.g., provide logs/metrics for the prior 90 days on request).

We attached a short redline the legal team suggested in-line in the PDF — feel free to ignore or incorporate as you see fit.

Laura

--
Attachment: meditech_initial_sla_request.pdf (redlines) [pdf]
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Laura Chen <procurement@meditechsolutions.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum & order form language for Redwood deployment

Hi Laura / Vanessa — looping in technical details and the first-pass artifacts.

On the technical front:
- Dedicated + burst-to-hosted hybrid: supported. We can define a baseline reserved capacity block in the order form and an explicit burst policy (max burst QPS by region, throttling/backpressure behavior).
- Latency commitments: p95 <=250ms for single-request small/mid tokens is achievable on our standard-A model profile with dedicated pools; p99 for batched workloads depends on batch size — we will include a latency table mapping batch sizes to expected p95/p99 numbers using the token distribution you provided.
- Regional failover: we support failover across us-west-2 and us-east-1 with automated DNS-level routing and persistent KV cache warming strategies. MTTF (measured from detection to traffic reroute) estimate: 3-9 minutes depending on the failure class; we'll include the distinction between planned maintenance and unplanned outage in the exhibit.

Attached:
- redwood-draft-sla-exhibit-v1.docx (first-pass language for availability measurement, credit schedule, regional failover clause, and order form exhibit placeholders)
- uptime-evidence-matrix.xlsx (maps signals: NLB healthchecks, internal GPU-queue metrics, prefix cache hit ratios, and our uptime calculation)

Notes on evidence/audit: we can provide a 90-day rolling incident history and an API endpoint for uptime telemetry. For audit-grade logs we will coordinate a SOC2-plus export with our compliance team — we will mark any sensitive redactions required.

Vanessa/Naomi: next steps from our side — Ops will finalize the evidence matrix (v1) by EOD 6/15, legal will incorporate procurement redlines into the exhibit and return v1 by 6/17. Vanessa: can you confirm the exact HubSpot record and procurement contact for DocuSign routing?

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Products & Operations
Redwood Inference
